title: Automated Technical Documentation Retrieval for Aerospace Engineering
business: Aerospace engineering firms managing vast repositories of legacy technical manuals and maintenance logs.
problem: Engineers struggle to locate relevant maintenance procedures because traditional keyword-based search fails to capture the intent behind natural language queries, leading to inefficient manual browsing of thousands of documents.
solution: By utilizing Sentence-BERT (SBERT) to transform textual documentation into fixed-length vector embeddings, the system enables semantic search. Instead of matching exact keywords, the system calculates the cosine similarity between the vector representation of a user's query and the pre-computed vectors of the document database, allowing for retrieval based on the underlying meaning of the technical request.
steps: Pre-process the corpus of technical manuals into individual sentence segments.
Pass each segment through a Siamese BERT-network to generate high-dimensional vector embeddings.
Store these embeddings in a vector database for efficient retrieval.
Convert incoming user queries into the same vector space using the identical SBERT model.
Perform a cosine similarity search to identify the most relevant document segments.
outcome: Engineers achieve faster access to precise maintenance instructions by querying with natural language, significantly reducing the time spent navigating legacy documentation.
limitation: A primary limitation is the loss of nuance in highly specialized technical jargon if the model was not fine-tuned on domain-specific aerospace corpora. This can be checked by evaluating the top-k retrieval results against a gold-standard set of manually curated relevant documents to identify false positives.

questions.question: In Automated Technical Documentation Retrieval for Aerospace Engineering, why is semantic search preferred over keyword search?
options: It captures the intent behind natural language queries.
It requires less computational power than keyword matching.
It eliminates the need for a vector database.
It guarantees 100% accuracy for all technical jargon.
questions.explanation: The problem states that keyword search fails to capture intent, which semantic search addresses by focusing on meaning.

questions.question: In Automated Technical Documentation Retrieval for Aerospace Engineering, what is a potential limitation of the implementation?
options: The system cannot handle more than ten documents.
The model may struggle with specialized jargon if not fine-tuned.
Cosine similarity is too slow for real-time retrieval.
SBERT requires the entire document to be re-indexed for every query.
questions.explanation: The limitation section explicitly mentions the risk of losing nuance in specialized jargon if the model lacks domain-specific training.
questions.evidence: A primary limitation is the loss of nuance in highly specialized technical jargon if the model was not fine-tuned on domain-specific aerospace corpora.
